a:r.a:t: Linkage of SNPs to Disease Inheritance

p:cNvPr.descr: 3 diagrams, including 2 pedigrees and a chromosome diagram, showing the presence of disease genes. (a) 2 pedigree charts show the presence of disease genes. The top diagram is the L family (labeled top left). The shapes on the pedigree chart are diamonds and can be either red or white. They can have either a diagonal line going through them, or none. The two parent diamonds, at the top, consist of one red lined diamond and one white slashed diamond. The red diamond is on the left is labeled 41. Their offspring are below. On the far left end are 48, which is red slashed and 77, which is white slashed. To the right, in the center of the line, is 36, which is red and slashed. To the right are four more individuals: 48, which is red and slashed, an unlabeled white slashed diamond as the mate; and 84 and 78, which are both white and lined. Below and to the left are the offspring of 48 and 77. From the left, they are 43 (red, slashed) mated left to a white slashed diamond. To the right is 63, white; 30, which is red and slashed, and its mate, which is unlabeled and white and slashed. To the right is 45, which is red and slashed; 58, which is white and slashed; 41, which is red and slashed; 58, which is white and slashed; 41, which is red and slashed; 56, which is white and slashed; 39, which is red and slashed; 53, 49, and 41, which are white; 44, which is red; and 39, which is red and slashed. To the right are the offspring of 48 and its mate. There are 4 offspring: 39, which is red and slashed; 40 and 41, which is red; and 41, which is white. To the left, 43 and its mate have 45, a single red offspring; to the right, 30 and its mate have a single offspring, 47, which is red. Below is the pedigree for the SNW family. One parent at the top is red, the other is white. Both are slashed. Below is a long line of all the offspring and their mates. From the left, the offspring are D61 (red, slashed) mated to a white slash; D61 (red, slashed) mated to a white slash; D57 (red, slashed) mated to a white slash; D59 (red, slashed) mated to a white slash; D50 (white slashed), mated to a white slash. To the lower left, the offspring of the leftmost D61 are D66 (red, slashed) mated to white; the offspring of the right D61 are D64 (red, slashed), mated to white; D60 (red, slashed), and 52 (red, slashed). The offspring of D57, to the right, are 80 (white) and 54 (red, slashed). To the right, the offspring of 59 are 48 (red, slashed), D53 (red, slashed) mated to white, D51 (red, slashed), D53 (red, slashed), 67 (white). To the far right, the offspring of D50 is 56 (red). The last level contains the great-grand offspring of the initial pair. To the left, the offspring of D66 are 73 (white), 50 (red), 76 (white), D56 (red, slashed), and 72 (white). To the right, the single offspring of D64 is red. To the right of this, the offspring of D53 is 50 (red, slashed) and 50 (white). B) A diagram of chromosome 14, oriented vertically. It is tan and white banded. The top portion of the chromosome is shorter; the bottom portion is long. A series of numbers from the top down has the following sequence: 13, 12, 11.2, 11.1, 11.1, 11.2, 12, 13, 21, 22, 23, 24.1, 24.2, 24.3, 31, 32.1, 32.2, 32.3. On the right are the chromosome marker positions. They are on a vertical number line with values on either side. A large white band around marker 11.2 is bracketed and labeled (TCRD) on the left side of the number line, with D14S50 on the right. On the right side of the number line are codes beginning with D. On the left side are numerical values that fall between the code values. The values and codes will be listed alternatively, as they appear on the number line. D codes appear on the right side, number values appear on the left side of the chromosome: D14S50, 16.1, D14S54, 7.5, D14D49, 11.7, D14S47, 12.6, D14S52, 20.7, D14S43, 2.5 (bracketed at white band 24.3) D14S53, 9.2, D14S55, 1.6, D14S48, 13.5, P1 (AACT) (bracketed at white band 32.1), 5.6, and D14S51, D14S1(bracketed at tan band 32.2). (c) The bottom diagram shows a region of interest on a particular chromosome. The chromosome is represented as a number line, with an arrow on the left end labeled “to telomere” and a label on the right labeled “to centromere.” The markers on the chromosome are indicated by marks on the line. Beginning on the left, the first marker is D14S53, then D14S61. The bracketed region of interest, labeled below, begins with D14S76, then D14S43/71 (this marker is higher than the others), D14S77 (slightly lower), then D14S277 (normal height), then D14S268. To the right is D14S289, then D14S258 at the far right end. Down below are several short green rods representing the markers. There is a single longer orange marker, labeled S182. To the lower right is a scale that reads, “1 Mb”, then approximately a 2-inch horizontal line, then underneath, “approximate scale.”
